summary.text: 你 means “you,” usually addressing one person. Its visible form combines 亻, representing a person, with 尔; treating 尔 as a sound element is a plausible but disputed analysis.

formation.text: A plausible analysis is phonosemantic: 亻 supplies the person category and 尔 a sound cue. A competing account reads 人 and 尔 together as “person” and “you.” The construction remains disputed because the available historical accounts do not directly establish how 你 was formed.

components.text: The left-side form 亻 represents a person and contributes the semantic category in the proposed phonosemantic analysis. It is the positional form of 人.
The right-side 尔 is proposed as the phonetic element. In its own graphic history, 尔 is described as a shortened form of 爾; that relationship does not prove its sound role in 你.

sound_limitation.text: The modern Mandarin readings ěr and nǐ can be compared, and the available Baxter–Sagart data gives 尔 as Middle Chinese nyeX and Old Chinese *n[ə][r]ʔ and 你 as Old Chinese *nɯʔ. This comparison does not establish 尔’s historical phonetic role in 你.

sound.text: In modern Mandarin, 尔 is ěr and 你 is nǐ. This comparison alone does not demonstrate the proposed historical sound relationship.

history.text: The dictionaries report 你 glossed as “you” in 集韻 and cite its use in 隋書. The earliest surviving written example and the date of the quoted wording remain unresolved. A small-seal-style rendering of 你 is a modern font construction, not an ancient form.

尔 is described as a shortened form of 爾, which was used for “you/your.” This is the graphic and word history of 尔; it neither establishes that 尔 depicts an object nor explains its proposed sound function in 你.

uncertainties.text: The phonosemantic and ideographic analyses of 你 are both reported, but no supplied historical account directly establishes its construction. The proposed sound analysis should therefore be treated as plausible, not certain.
No original depicted object or independently recoverable object-name pronunciation for 尔 is established, so an account of 你 as a borrowing from an object-name is unsupported.
Plural, possessive, and generic uses are listed, but their dates and semantic links to the singular pronoun are unresolved.

senses.text: The dictionaries cite 你 with the gloss 汝也 (“you”) and give second-person examples. These attest the use, but do not establish its exact earliest surviving occurrence or the date of the quoted wording.
The character dictionaries also record plural, possessive, and generic uses, without establishing when they arose or how they relate to the singular pronoun.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish a chronology or semantic development linking the reported plural, possessive, and generic uses to the singular second-person pronoun.

overview.text: 你 means “you,” usually addressing one person. One analysis treats 尔 as a sound cue in the compound, but modern Mandarin ěr and nǐ alone do not establish a historical sound match; the analysis remains disputed.

components.text: 亻 represents a person and contributes that category in the proposed analysis; it is the side form of 人.
尔 is proposed as a sound cue. Its modern reading ěr can be compared with 你 nǐ, but that pair does not prove a historical link.

relationships.text: In the proposed analysis of 你, 亻 represents a person and contributes the semantic category.

One analysis proposes 尔 as the sound element. The modern Mandarin readings are ěr and nǐ, but the supplied evidence does not establish a historical sound relation; another analysis treats the parts ideographically.
